### ① Derived judgments

- Ratchet rows equal the measured head: SKILL.md 321 (main 320), `lanes/objectstack.md` 35, table-row pin 0 (the charter has no table). Right.
- SKILL.md 域车道: the new row is 212 B; the widest row stays 341 B, pin unmoved. Right.
- Charter lines are at most 118 B, the project-forms line 113 B; no 3-digit `#` id and no quotation in the three prose files. Right.
- `repo:objectstack` needs no lane-grammar edit (`SIGNATURE_LANE_SOURCE` admits `repo:` plus a slug); the seat word reaches project-forms. Right.
- Check-runs on this head when read: 16 success, 28 skipped, 7 in progress (among them `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`), 1 failure: `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`, completed 15:00:50Z, before the claim comment of 15:01:30Z; its log was not read. `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and `Check Changeset` are success. The gate verdicts are NOT yet complete.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` fits: all four paths sit under `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**`, nothing published. Clause-②: no, as the claim declares.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Land order: the claim puts PR 33938 first. Charter L19 points at a stay-in-lane and notify rule that exists only at that PR's head (3fbadcf6), not on main; if the order flips, L19 points at nothing. The section name it cites survives in both versions.
- The SKILL.md raise cites the lane ruling quoted in the card body, in the neighbouring 319 to 320 shape, minus a comment id. The words order a lane, not a line; the Tier H approval is the consent. Named for the maintainer.

### ④ Design judgment

M1 (must-fix) — charter L26 tells seats to write area names and path roots into the takes/leaves of `Notify: split`. The key's owner refuses that: `readList` in `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` reads `none` or `#n` card numbers only, so every such line is unreadable, and the key's own `when` is round open on a changed card list. The lane's one new exclusion mechanism rides on a line the reader rejects. Fix in prose: keep the template, let the lease table carry area and paths; or card a recogniser change first.

S1 (should-fix) — L28 arbitrates a double claim by the seat post's edit stamp. Not in the card; area-lease rewrites the table on any column change, so the stamp moves; `seat-lifecycle.md` already owns the race rule (audit-comment timestamp, first come) and forbids reading the post's `updated_at`. Point there.

S2 (should-fix) — L29 ends in an unqualified ban on file exclusivity. `execution-duties.md` keeps `SINGLE_CLAIM_PATHS` exclusive and the PR-body guard enforces it; the rule is stronger than the tree allows. Carve the single-writer paths out by pointer. Its own home (the merge-tree script card) is not landed.

S3 (should-fix) — restated rules, against the card's own promise to point and not copy: L34 second half copies area-lease (main L46, 33938 L52) with its 3,000 figure; L17 copies project-forms L42 and the SKILL.md cloud row, and is not in the card; L18 copies area-lease (main L37, 33938 L32), widened from area to seat, the only part the card orders.

Nits:
- L35: concurrency set by the maintainer, and Chinese reporting, are not in the card; the latter is a 33938 rule.
- L24 seat-prefixed area names: not in the card, a sound mechanism; no reader of `lease:` label shape exists to break.
- L10 closes the seat relabel of `execution-duties.md` without naming it; faithful to the card.
- L11: the label is retired from circulation per `ensure-pm-labels.sh`, not a live seam label; the H14 reading is as cited.
- L30: the taking seat rewrites two lease tables, one on a post it does not sit on; say who writes the leaving seat's.
- L27 override of the odd/even alternation points at the right line and follows from the card.
- project-forms now admits every `lanes/` file as a seat word (cloud, security newly); wider than the card's one word, harmless.

Faithful to the card otherwise: seat form, multi-account, not a single-lane-repo seat, triage keeps `domain:*`, no label on cards, cloud and security carve-outs, one area one seat.
